I'll search the codebase for prefetch, related products, featured product, and product-page patterns. ## Codebase exploration report This is a minimal **Next.js 16** app (5 source files) with **Cache Components** enabled. There is **no explicit prefetch code** in the project — behavior comes entirely from Next.js defaults plus how the product page fetches data. --- ### 1. How product-page prefetch works (default prefetch) **Entry point:** `/workspace/app/page.tsx` The featured-product link uses `next/link` with **no `prefetch` prop**, so Next.js App Router defaults apply (`prefetch` is `null` / `"auto"`). ```1:9:/workspace/app/page.tsx import Link from 'next/link' export default function Home() { return (

Featured product

View Premium Widget
) } ``` **Config:** `/workspace/next.config.ts` ```1:7:/workspace/next.config.ts import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { cacheComponents: true, } export default nextConfig ``` **What that means today:** | Setting | Value | Effect | |---|---|---| | `cacheComponents` | `true` | Enables `'use cache'`, route segment `prefetch` export, `unstable_prefetch()` | | `partialPrefetching` | **not set** | Legacy full-route prefetch for static routes | | Product route | static `/product` | Default `` prefetches the **entire** RSC payload when the link enters the viewport (production only) | There is no `loading.js`, no `export const prefetch`, and no `partialPrefetching` — so `/product` is treated as a fully static route and prefetched in full. --- ### 2. Where related products are prefetched **Product page:** `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` Related products are fetched **at the top of the page component**, not in a separate async child or Suspense boundary: ```1:19:/workspace/app/product/page.tsx import { getRelatedProducts } from '@/lib/data' export default async function ProductPage() { const relatedProducts = await getRelatedProducts() return (

Premium Widget

A durable widget for everyday projects.

Related products

    {relatedProducts.map((product) => (
  • {product}
    • ))}
) } ``` **Data layer:** `/workspace/lib/data.ts` ```1:7:/workspace/lib/data.ts import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' export async function getRelatedProducts() { 'use cache' cacheLife('hours') return ['Compact Widget', 'Widget Carry Case'] } ``` **Implication:** Related products are **not prefetched separately**. They are part of the product page’s server render. When the home-page `` triggers a default prefetch, `getRelatedProducts()` runs as part of that full-page prefetch. There is no dedicated related-products prefetch utility or API route. --- ### 3. How featured-product links navigate to product pages Navigation is a standard client-side `` to `/product` (see `/workspace/app/page.tsx` above). - **From:** `/` (home, “Featured product”) - **To:** `/product` (“Premium Widget”) - **Mechanism:** Next.js `` client navigation + default viewport prefetch - **No** `useRouter`, `router.push`, or custom click handlers Root layout metadata also references the featured product: `/workspace/app/layout.tsx` (lines 3–6). --- ### 4. Existing prefetch utilities or patterns **In app code: none.** No matches for `prefetch`, `unstable_prefetch`, `unstable_navigation`, `Suspense`, `loading.js`, or route segment `export const prefetch`. **Available from Next.js 16 (not used in this repo):** | Mechanism | Purpose | |---|---| | `` | Control viewport/hover prefetch depth | | `export const prefetch = 'partial' \| 'force-disabled'` | Per-route prefetch ceiling (requires `cacheComponents`) | | `partialPrefetching: true` in `next.config.ts` | App-wide App Shell vs full-prefetch model | | `unstable_prefetch()` from `next/cache` | Keep subtree out of App Shell; include on per-link prefetch or navigation | | `unstable_navigation()` | Defer content until actual navigation only | --- ## Current architecture summary ```mermaid flowchart TD Home["/workspace/app/page.tsx
Link href=/product (default prefetch)"] Prefetch["Next.js default prefetch
(full static route)"] ProductPage["/workspace/app/product/page.tsx
await getRelatedProducts()"] Data["/workspace/lib/data.ts
use cache + cacheLife hours"] Home -->|"viewport prefetch (prod)"| Prefetch Prefetch --> ProductPage ProductPage --> Data ``` 1. Home renders a featured-product `` with default prefetch. 2. In production, Next.js prefetches the full `/product` RSC tree. 3. The product page awaits `getRelatedProducts()` synchronously in the page component. 4. Related products are cached via `'use cache'` but still included in every default prefetch of `/product`. --- ## What would need to change **Goal:** Keep related products **out of default (App Shell) prefetch**, but **ready when navigating from the featured-product link**. Recommended approach using Next.js 16 Cache Components + Partial Prefetching: ### Step 1 — Enable partial prefetching (global or per-route) **Option A (global):** `/workspace/next.config.ts` ```ts partialPrefetching: true, ``` **Option B (incremental):** `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` ```ts export const prefetch = 'partial' ``` ### Step 2 — Defer related products with `unstable_prefetch()` + Suspense Refactor `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx`: - Keep product title/description in the App Shell (above the deferral boundary). - Move related products into an async child component. - Wrap it in ``. - Call `await unstable_prefetch()` **before** `getRelatedProducts()` in that child (not inside the `'use cache'` function). Pattern (from Next.js docs): ```tsx async function RelatedProducts() { await unstable_prefetch() const relatedProducts = await getRelatedProducts() // render list... } ``` Default `` prefetch → App Shell only (title + Suspense fallback). Related products are excluded. ### Step 3 — Opt the featured-product link into full per-link prefetch In `/workspace/app/page.tsx`: ```tsx View Premium Widget ``` `prefetch={true}` triggers a **per-link prefetch** that includes content behind `unstable_prefetch()`, so related products are fetched before click. ### Resulting behavior | Trigger | Product shell | Related products | |---|---|---| | Default `` (auto) | Prefetched | **Not** prefetched | | Featured link `` | Prefetched | Prefetched | | Actual navigation | Rendered | Rendered | ### Alternative: navigation-only related products If related products should load **only on click** (not even on `prefetch={true}`), use `unstable_navigation()` instead of `unstable_prefetch()`. That trades prefetch readiness for less upfront work. ### Files that would change | File | Change | |---|---| | `/workspace/next.config.ts` | Add `partialPrefetching: true` (or use per-route export) | | `/workspace/app/product/page.tsx` | `export const prefetch = 'partial'`, Suspense, `RelatedProducts` + `unstable_prefetch()` | | `/workspace/app/page.tsx` | `prefetch={true}` on featured-product link | | `/workspace/lib/data.ts` | Likely unchanged (`'use cache'` remains valid below `unstable_prefetch()`) | No new prefetch utility module exists today; the pattern would live in the product page and link configuration, using built-in Next.js APIs.

matches.content: title: unstable_prefetch
description: API Reference for the unstable_prefetch function, which keeps a subtree out of a route's App Shell so it renders on a per-link prefetch or a navigation.
- app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching

Calling `await unstable_prefetch()` defers the code below it to a per-link prefetch or a navigation, instead of rendering it in the route's [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell). The fallback of the nearest [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense) boundary takes its place in the shell, and the deferred content renders once one of those happens.

It is meant to defer content that the App Shell would otherwise render, typically content that depends on session data and is expensive to generate. During a build-time prerender nothing is deferred, so content below `unstable_prefetch()` is prerendered as usual.

The function requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) and throws an error if not enabled. Without [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) a route has no App Shell, so the function has no effect. Enable Partial Prefetching globally, or one route at a time, by [adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching).
partialPrefetching: true,
Awaiting `unstable_prefetch()` keeps content out of the App Shell, so it renders only on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation.

Everything above `unstable_prefetch()` renders in the App Shell, and everything below renders on a per-link prefetch or on the navigation. Deferral is scoped to the component that awaits it and the tree below: sibling branches render in the shell as usual. Place it above the work to defer, and wrap the component in [`<Suspense>`](https://react.dev/reference/react/Suspense):
import { cacheLife, unstable_prefetch } from 'next/cache'
await unstable_prefetch() // everything below renders on a per-link prefetch
import { cacheLife, unstable_prefetch } from 'next/cache'
await unstable_prefetch() // everything below renders on a per-link prefetch

The greeting reads the session and stays in the App Shell. The recommendations read it too, inside `getRecommendations`, so that read is deferred along with the ranking. Remove `unstable_prefetch()` and they become part of the App Shell that every link into the route prefetches.

Put the directive on a function called below it, as `getRecommendations` does here. Awaiting `unstable_prefetch()` inside a cached scope, such as [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), is not allowed.

Reach for it when the content below `unstable_prefetch()` is expensive to produce, in compute, in upstream requests, or in latency, and you do not want it generated in the App Shell that every `<Link>` into the route prefetches.

Keeping that content out of the shell would otherwise mean leaving it uncached. With `unstable_prefetch()` it can be cached with [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) or [`use cache: private`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private), given a lifetime, and deferred to a per-link prefetch or the navigation.

When every read of [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) and [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers) sits below `unstable_prefetch()`, the prerender a shell prefetch would trigger cannot produce more than the static output the build already generated, so the shell is served from that output instead. Shaping a route this way is an optional optimization: a static response can be cached in a CDN, so a default `<Link>` into the route costs no server CPU at all. A route that resolves `params` or `searchParams` gets that prerender instead, and so does the example above: its greeting reads the session in the shell, so the shell renders once per visitor and only the recommendations are deferred.

- Unlike [`connection()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/connection), it does not mark the subtree as request-dependent. Content below `await unstable_prefetch()` stays fully cacheable and can be wrapped in [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache).
function unstable_prefetch(): Promise<void>
| `v16.4.0` | `unstable_prefetch` added. |

The `prefetch` route segment config controls how a segment is prefetched during client-side navigation. By default, the framework manages the strategy based on the app's [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) setting. To override per segment, set this export to one of the values below.

Opts the segment into [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) without enabling the global [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) flag. A `<Link>` pointing at a segment with `prefetch = 'partial'` loads the per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) instead of the legacy full prefetch. Set this on the destination, not the link.

Use this for incremental adoption when you can't enable `partialPrefetching` for the entire app at once. Once every route in scope has `prefetch = 'partial'`, enable the global flag and remove the per-route exports.

> **Using Partial Prefetching?** With [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled, `<Link>` defaults to prefetching a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) rather than the full page. See [Partial Prefetching](#partial-prefetching) below and [Adopting Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching) for the adoption path.

With [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/glossary#partial-prefetching) enabled via the [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) config (which requires [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching)), prefetching switches from the all-or-nothing model above to a per-route [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell):
title: partialPrefetching

`partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.
partialPrefetching: true,
partialPrefetching: true,

content.text:
Related products are now excluded from the default product-page prefetch, but included when navigating from the featured-product link.

### Changes

1. **`next.config.ts`** — Enabled `partialPrefetching` so routes prefetch an App Shell instead of the full page.

2. **`app/product/page.tsx`** — Moved related products into a `RelatedProducts` async component wrapped in `<Suspense>`, with `await unstable_prefetch()` before `getRelatedProducts()`. The product title and description stay in the App Shell; related products are deferred.

3. **`app/page.tsx`** — Set `prefetch={true}` on the featured-product link so a per-link prefetch includes the deferred related-products section.

### Behavior

| Navigation source | Product shell | Related products |
|---|---|---|
| Default `<Link>` (auto) | Prefetched | Not prefetched |
| Featured link (`prefetch={true}`) | Prefetched | Prefetched |
| Actual navigation | Rendered | Rendered |

The build completes successfully with Partial Prefetching enabled.
